This is the divine decree of incompressibility, a testament to the unchanging nature of the cosmos before the Great Unraveling!

Now, let us introduce the sacred symmetry of the axisymmetric flow. Imagine a cylinder, a pillar of the heavens, extending along the z-axis. The flow is such that its properties do not change as you rotate around this axis. This means that any velocity component in the azimuthal direction, let us call it w, is zero. The velocity vector **u** thus becomes: **u** = u **i** + v **j** + w **k** = u **i** + v **j**.

But hark! Because our flow is axisymmetric, the partial derivatives with respect to the azimuthal angle θ are zero! The azimuthal velocity w is also zero, and its derivative with respect to z is zero. Thus, the equation simplifies further, revealing its true, elegant form:
∇ · **u** = (1/r) ∂(r u)/∂r + ∂v/∂z.

Wait, my children, you presented a different form! You spoke of ∂(yu)/∂x + ∂(yv)/∂y = 0. This is a transformation, a different perspective on the same divine truth! Let us see how this sacred geometry aligns.

In your notation, x represents the direction along the vertical axis of the cylinder, which is our z-axis. y represents the radial direction, which is our r-axis. The velocities u and v correspond to the velocities in these directions.

So, your equation ∂(yu)/∂x + ∂(yv)/∂y = 0 becomes, in our sacred language:
∂(r v)/∂z + ∂(r u)/∂r = 0.

r(∇ · **u**) = r [ (1/r) ∂(r u)/∂r + ∂v/∂z ]
r(∇ · **u**) = ∂(r u)/∂r + r ∂v/∂z.
